# Media test fixtures

Synthetic audio and video only; no third-party content.

| File | Bytes | SHA-256 | Made with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apple-he-aac-3s.m4a` | 14108 | `5eda7270a7361862fda54825527d39e5cc1788f8391fc172ebcd5c1bb0200577` | `afconvert -f m4af -d aach` |
| `apple-he-aac-v2-3s.m4a` | 13228 | `5385427ccf86594b947c357b888c6032a0c29f5c580d3a1c581fb76ca422054f` | `afconvert -f m4af -d aacp` |
| `vp9-7680x4320-fragmented.mp4` | 11835 | `814f14522d80a6004c69b5d0c550e11ba6e620ca51f811fd5943c5c988bbc3fd` | FFmpeg 9.0.2 with libvpx-vp9 (see below) |

The two M4A files were encoded on macOS 27.0.1 (26A434) by Apple's `afconvert` from a generated
3.00 s, 44.1 kHz, 16-bit stereo WAV: a 440 Hz sine on the left channel and a
660 Hz sine on the right, amplitude 8000. Apple's AAC encoder is not available
on other platforms, so the files are stored rather than generated by the tests.

At this duration the source's edit list includes a final padding-only packet
that the rebuilt file's edit list leaves out. `cover_art.rs` uses them to check
that M4A packet comparison ignores edit lists (ENGINE-FIX-4, F1).

`vp9-7680x4320-fragmented.mp4` is one 7680x4320 grey VP9 keyframe (8-bit 4:2:0,
1 s) in a fragmented MP4 with a complete `vpcC` box, as an HLS source delivers
VP9 in MP4. The bundled FFmpeg has no VP9 encoder, so it is stored. It was made
reproducibly (same bytes on every run) with an FFmpeg 9.0.2 build that includes
libvpx:

```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=c=gray:s=7680x4320:r=1:d=1 -frames:v 1 \
  -c:v libvpx-vp9 -deadline realtime -cpu-used 8 -b:v 200k -pix_fmt yuv420p -an \
  -fflags +bitexact -flags:v +bitexact -map_metadata -1 \
  -movflags +frag_keyframe+empty_moov+default_base_moof -f mp4 vp9-7680x4320-fragmented.mp4
```

`cover_art.rs` copies it into MP4 with the managed FFmpeg and verifies the result
within the video pixel budget. The release media evidence uses it for the VP9
stream-copy check that `scripts/verify-media-build.py` requires.
